statement: Both baseline checks rest on growth rates of iterated linear maps or expansions: P97's life-cycle fitness is the log dominant eigenvalue of a projection matrix (confirmed by iteration to 1e-8), and P98's sanity measures how fast the digits of an expansion pin a number down; both separate a short-run quantity from a long-run one.

All three audited self-transcendence studies have printed numbers that do not follow from their own inputs (P99's Power mean and participant flow; P100's chance agreement and Bartlett df; P101's vastness BF01 and wording), while their main test statistics reproduce.

Experiences described as transcending the self are studied through reports: P101's sublime ratings and P102's mystics' accounts; the PHI toy shows report agreement can arise from a shared background as well as from a common core. Analogy, not a shared mechanism.

Transcendence as a transition to a new level of individuality differs from ascent within one landscape: P97's tradeoff breaking moves the feasible set rather than climbing within it (TR0-NAT-02, both F and f2 rise). No ordering of phases is assumed; the owner's level mapping is not tested.

Recomputing test statistics from printed summaries catches reporting slips in self-transcendence studies: P103's life-satisfaction p is .047 not .470, and P101's vastness Bayes factor is printed as its reciprocal in the text; default Bayes factors also separate strong from weak evidence where one-tailed p values near .04 do not.

Composite or aggregate agreement can hide structure: self-transcendence values do not rank SVO groups the same way for Universalism and Benevolence, and in the mysticism toy agreement across traditions does not reveal whether it comes from a common core or a shared heritage. Analogy, not a shared mechanism.
